name: Starship Demo
vehicle: Starship (Super Heavy + Starship upper stage, expended)
first: First fully reusable launch system to attempt Mars landing
description: An uncrewed demonstration of the Starship Mars architecture: launch on Super Heavy, refill in LEO from a tanker variant, then trans-Mars injection of a fully-fuelled Starship and powered descent to the Martian surface. SpaceX aimed for the late-2026 Mars window. In February 2026 Elon Musk put the Moon first and said work on Mars would start in about five to seven years, dropping the late-2026 target; no new date has been set. A Mars Starship would land about a hundred tonnes at a time, against a few thousand kilograms for today's landers.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Starship from Boca Chica or Cape Canaveral — first super-heavy interplanetary launch.

events.label: ORBITAL REFILLING
events.note: Tanker rendezvous and propellant transfer in LEO over multiple flights.

events.label: TMI BURN
events.note: Trans-Mars injection from fully-fuelled LEO state.

events.label: MARS LANDING
events.note: Powered descent to Mars surface — no parachutes, no airbags, no sky-crane.
